answer:
To draw the development of the lateral surface of the cut cylinder:

1. **Projections of the Cylinder:**
   - Draw the top view (circle of diameter $30\text{ mm}$) and divide it into 12 equal parts (1, 2, 3, ... 12).
   - Draw the front view (rectangle of $30\text{ mm}$ base and $50\text{ mm}$ height).

2. **Apply the Section Plane:**
   - The section plane passes through the top end of an extreme generator and is inclined at $45^\circ$ to H.P.
   - Draw this line at $45^\circ$ starting from the top corner of the extreme generator in the front view.

3. **Development Construction:**
   - Draw a straight baseline equal to the circumference of the cylinder ($CD = \pi d = \pi \times 30 \approx 94.2\text{ mm}$). Divide this line into 12 equal parts and erect vertical generators.
   - Project horizontal lines from the points where the section plane intersects each generator in the front view to the corresponding vertical generators in the development.
   - Connect these intersection points with a smooth curve and shade the required lateral surface below the curve.
proTip: Remember that the development of a cylinder is a rectangle whose width equals the perimeter ($\pi D$) and height equals the height of the cylinder.
